title: Add features to an inventory class (medium, one module)
command:
Extend the Inventory class in inventory.py. Keep existing behavior and signatures.
1. low_stock(threshold) -> list of SKUs whose quantity is strictly below threshold, sorted by quantity ascending, then SKU.
2. import_csv(text) -> list[str]. text is CSV with header `sku,name,qty,price` (extra surrounding whitespace in cells is ignored). Each valid row is applied like add(). Invalid rows are skipped and reported as `line N: <reason>` where N is the 1-based line number in the text (the header is line 1). A row is invalid if a field is missing or empty, qty is not a non-negative integer, price is not a non-negative number, or the SKU already exists with a different name. Blank lines are ignored. Return the error list (empty when all rows are valid).
3. undo() -> bool: revert the most recent successful add(), remove() or import_csv() (an import is undone as a whole, and is not recorded at all if it applied no rows). Repeated calls go further back. Returns False when there is nothing to undo.
4. to_json() -> str and classmethod from_json(text) -> Inventory that round-trip all items (sku, name, qty, price). Undo history is not saved.
5. total_value() returns the sum of qty*price rounded to 2 decimals (it currently ignores quantity).
